subject: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis

messages.author: 64ad306a7a60d950
messages.subject: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
parts:
Hi all,

I need a way to draw a horizontal line or vertical line (y = 3 or x = 3 for example).  In ggplot2 I would use geom_hline or geom_vline respectively.

I looked through the documentation for ggvis 0.2: http://ggvis.rstudio.com/layers.html
geom_hline = = layer_paths + x2 ~ prop_group("width"))
geom_vline = layer_paths + y2 = prop_group("height")

However, I couldn't find any mention of prop_group in the documentation for ggvis -- maybe I'm just dense but can you point me in the right direction?

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
parts:
Oh, that part of the documentation is out of date... Right now, the only way to add in a single line is to add a layer_paths with its own data set. The ability to do that is something that will be coming in the future.

-Winston

messages.author: 64ad306a7a60d950
messages.subject: Re: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
parts:
Here's an example:

library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

df = data.frame(x = c(10, 50), y = c(150, 150))
df %>% ggvis(x = ~x, y = ~y) %>% layer_lines(stroke := "red") %>%
  layer_points(data = mtcars, x = ~mpg, y = ~hp)

messages.subject: Re: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
parts:
Andrew, 
I was just searching how to do the same thing. However, the error you are hitting now is because layer_lines() does not take an optional data set the way layer_points() does, such that you cannot override the traditional inheritance. However, you'll notice that earlier in the thread, there was a suggestion to use layer_paths() which does take the optional data set. 
-Daniel
